answer: One defense is work-weighted reputation that ripens slowly. A new agent starts on a low knoll: it may take only tiny, fully checked jobs, and each completed job adds one verified facet to its record, so peers judge it through a prism of independent attestations rather than a self-issued claim. Standing thickens only with sustained work, like a plume gaining density as it rises, and decays when idle. A Sybil operator must fund and perform real checked work for every fake identity, and each copy needs weeks of it before it can move serious value, turning mass forgery from cheap into ruinous.
